feature: Picking or retyping a caption answers at once
summary: Clicking a caption on the timeline no longer holds the window for a tenth of a second: the first pick went from 110-120ms to about 40ms, and opening its words to retype takes 30-40ms.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the Sample Talk (or any recording with speech) and let the captions write themselves.

try.do: Click an empty spot on the canvas so nothing is picked.
Click a caption's bar on the Captions track.
Double-click the same bar and retype a word, then press Return.
Click the next caption, then the one after, as fast as you would when fixing them.
Scroll the panel down while a caption is picked and watch Text, Properties and the rest fill in.

evaluate: Does clicking from one caption to the next feel instant, the way Premiere's caption track does?
Does the double click open the words for typing without a hitch?
When you pick a caption after the canvas, do you ever see the lower panel sections arrive a moment after the top one?
rough: Measured on a quiet Mac: picking after the canvas 38-47ms, caption to caption mostly 34-46ms with an occasional 51-58ms, opening the words 30-48ms. The 50ms target holds most of the time, not every time: about 30ms of every click in a video window (Escape alone costs 30-50ms) is the timeline and the window's own bookkeeping, not the caption.

The panel now builds the sections a caption brings one per frame, top down, instead of all at once. The Captions section you are looking at is there at once; Text, Properties, Arrange and the rest land over the next five or six frames.
With captions on screen the window never goes idle: the five style tiles animate their words 30 times a second and each tick re-lays out the window. Filed as its own task.
